Lean.Expr.app.comment:
A function application.

For example, the natural number one, i.e. `Nat.succ Nat.zero` is represented as
``Expr.app (.const `Nat.succ []) (.const .zero [])``.
Note that multiple arguments are represented using partial application.

For example, the two argument application `f x y` is represented as
`Expr.app (.app f x) y`.
Lean.Expr.app.description: A representation of applying a function to an argument in an expression format.

Lean.Expr.const.description: A representation of a constant expression associated with a given declaration name and universal quantification levels.

Lean.mkSort.comment: `.sort u` is now the preferred form.
Lean.mkSort.description: A representation of a sort expression associated with a specified level.

Lean.mkApp.comment: `.app f a` is now the preferred form.
Lean.mkApp.fullDefinition: @[match_pattern] def mkApp (f a : Expr) : Expr :=   .app f a
Lean.mkApp.description: A representation of an application of a function to an argument in expression format.

Lean.Expr.isAppOfArity.comment:
Given `f a₁ ... aᵢ`, returns true if `f` is a constant
with name `n` and has the correct number of arguments.
Lean.Expr.isAppOfArity.fullDefinition: def isAppOfArity : Expr → Name → Nat → Bool   | const c _, n, 0   => c == n   | app f _,   n, a+1 => isAppOfArity f n a   | _,         _, _   => false
Lean.Expr.isAppOfArity.description: A function that checks if a given expression is an application of a constant with a specified name and the correct number of arguments.

Lean.Expr.fvar.comment:
The `fvar` constructor represent free variables. These *free* variable
occurrences are not bound by an earlier `lam`, `forallE`, or `letE`
constructor and its binder exists in a local context only.

Note that Lean uses the *locally nameless approach*. See [McBride and McKinna](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.365.2479&rep=rep1&type=pdf)
for additional details.

When "visiting" the body of a binding expression (i.e. `lam`, `forallE`, or `letE`),
bound variables are converted into free variables using a unique identifier,
and their user-facing name, type, value (for `LetE`), and binder annotation
are stored in the `LocalContext`.
Lean.Expr.fvar.description: A representation of a free variable in an expression that is not bound by any preceding binding constructors and exists only within a specific local context.

Lean.mkConst.fullDefinition: def mkConst (declName : Name) (us : List Level := []) : Expr :=   .const declName us
Lean.mkConst.description: A function that creates a constant expression given its declaration name and optional universe levels.

Lean.Expr.nat?.comment:
Checks if an expression is a "natural number numeral in normal form",
i.e. of type `Nat`, and explicitly of the form `OfNat.ofNat n`
where `n` matches `.lit (.natVal n)` for some literal natural number `n`.
and if so returns `n`.
Lean.Expr.nat?.fullDefinition: def nat? (e : Expr) : Option Nat := do   let_expr OfNat.ofNat _ n _ := e | failure   let lit (.natVal n) := n | failure   n
Lean.Expr.nat?.description: A function that checks if an expression represents a natural number in a specific normal form and returns the number if it does.

Lean.Expr.int?.comment:
Checks if an expression is an "integer numeral in normal form",
i.e. of type `Nat` or `Int`, and either a natural number numeral in normal form (as specified by `nat?`),
or the negation of a positive natural number numberal in normal form,
and if so returns the integer.
Lean.Expr.int?.fullDefinition: def int? (e : Expr) : Option Int :=   let_expr Neg.neg _ _ a := e | e.nat?   match a.nat? with   | none => none   | some 0 => none   | some n => some (-n)
Lean.Expr.int?.description: A function that checks if an expression represents an integer numeral in normal form and returns its value if it does.

Lean.mkRawNatLit.comment:
Return the "raw" natural number `.lit (.natVal n)`.
This is not the default representation used by the Lean frontend.
See `mkNatLit`.
Lean.mkRawNatLit.fullDefinition: def mkRawNatLit (n : Nat) : Expr :=   mkLit (.natVal n)
Lean.mkRawNatLit.description: A function that produces a representation of a natural number in its unprocessed literal form.

Lean.Expr.getRevArg!.fullDefinition: def getRevArg! : Expr → Nat → Expr   | app _ a, 0   => a   | app f _, i+1 => getRevArg! f i   | _,       _   => panic! "invalid index"
Lean.Expr.getRevArg!.description: A function that retrieves an argument from an expression based on its position in reverse order.

Lean.Expr.getAppFn.comment:
If the given expression is a sequence of
function applications `f a₁ .. aₙ`, return `f`.
Otherwise return the input expression.
Lean.Expr.getAppFn.fullDefinition: def getAppFn : Expr → Expr   | app f _ => getAppFn f   | e         => e
Lean.Expr.getAppFn.description: A function that retrieves the main function from a sequence of applied expressions or returns the input if it does not represent an application.

Lean.mkAppN.comment: `mkAppN f #[a₀, ..., aₙ]` constructs the application `f a₀ a₁ ... aₙ`.
Lean.mkAppN.fullDefinition: def mkAppN (f : Expr) (args : Array Expr) : Expr :=   args.foldl mkApp f
Lean.mkAppN.description: A function that constructs an expression representing the application of a given function to a specified array of arguments.

Lean.mkStrLit.fullDefinition: def mkStrLit (s : String) : Expr :=   mkLit (.strVal s)
Lean.mkStrLit.description: A representation of a string literal in expression format.

Lean.Expr.proj.comment:
Projection-expressions. They are redundant, but are used to create more compact
terms, speedup reduction, and implement eta for structures.
The type of `struct` must be an structure-like inductive type. That is, it has only one
constructor, is not recursive, and it is not an inductive predicate. The kernel and elaborators
check whether the `typeName` matches the type of `struct`, and whether the (zero-based) index
is valid (i.e., it is smaller than the number of constructor fields).
When exporting Lean developments to other systems, `proj` can be replaced with `typeName`.`rec`
applications.

Example, given `a : Nat × Bool`, `a.1` is represented as
```
.proj `Prod 0 a
```
Lean.Expr.proj.description: A function that generates a projection expression for accessing fields of structure-like types, ensuring the provided type name and index are valid.

Lean.Expr.withApp.code: Lean.Expr.withApp.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} (e : Expr) (k : Expr → Array Expr → α) : α
Lean.Expr.withApp.comment: Given `e = f a₁ a₂ ... aₙ`, returns `k f #[a₁, ..., aₙ]`.
Lean.Expr.withApp.fullDefinition: @[inline] def withApp (e : Expr) (k : Expr → Array Expr → α) : α :=   let dummy := mkSort levelZero   let nargs := e.getAppNumArgs   withAppAux k e (mkArray nargs dummy) (nargs-1)
Lean.Expr.withApp.description: A function that deconstructs an expression representing a function application into the function and its arguments, then applies a given handler to them.

Lean.Expr.beta.comment:
Apply the given arguments to `f`, beta-reducing if `f` is a
lambda expression. See docstring for `betaRev` for examples.
Lean.Expr.beta.fullDefinition: def beta (f : Expr) (args : Array Expr) : Expr :=   betaRev f args.reverse
Lean.Expr.beta.description: A function that applies given arguments to an expression, beta-reducing it if the expression is a lambda.

Lean.Expr.mvar.comment:
Metavariables are used to represent "holes" in expressions, and goals in the
tactic framework. Metavariable declarations are stored in the `MetavarContext`.
Metavariables are used during elaboration, and are not allowed in the kernel,
or in the code generator.
Lean.Expr.mvar.description: A representation of a metavariable in an expression that signifies an unfilled placeholder or a goal in the tactic framework, utilized during the process of elaboration.

Lean.BinderInfo.default.description: A representation of the standard binder information used for variables in type annotations.

Lean.BinderInfo.implicit.description: An annotation indicating that a binder is implicit, such as those used in parameter lists of functions.

Lean.BinderInfo.strictImplicit.comment: Strict implicit binder annotation, e.g., `{{ x : α }}`
Lean.BinderInfo.strictImplicit.description: A specification of a strict implicit binder annotation used to indicate that a variable is implicitly bound in certain contexts.

Lean.BinderInfo.instImplicit.comment: Local instance binder annotataion, e.g., `[Decidable α]`
Lean.BinderInfo.instImplicit.description: A specification of an implicit binder used to annotate local instances, such as in the context of decidable types.

Lean.Expr.mvarId!.fullDefinition: def mvarId! : Expr → MVarId   | mvar n => n   | _      => panic! "mvar expected"
Lean.Expr.mvarId!.description: A function that extracts the metavariable identifier from an expression.

Lean.Expr.replaceFVars.code: Lean.Expr.replaceFVars (e : Expr) (fvars vs : Array Expr) : Expr
Lean.Expr.replaceFVars.comment: Replace occurrences of the free variables `fvars` in `e` with `vs`
Lean.Expr.replaceFVars.fullDefinition: def replaceFVars (e : Expr) (fvars : Array Expr) (vs : Array Expr) : Expr :=   (e.abstract fvars).instantiateRev vs
Lean.Expr.replaceFVars.description: A function that replaces specified free variables in an expression with given replacement expressions.
